title: Truncated sections detect the conormal kernel modulo the maximal ideal
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings in Type u, with an R-algebra structure on S, and assume S is local. Let C be a local commutative R-algebra with a surjective R-algebra map C -> S. Put J = ker(C -> S), m the unique maximal ideal of C and n the unique maximal ideal of S. Let N >= 2 satisfy m^N intersect J contained in mJ. Suppose the canonical quotient map C/(J^2 + m^N) -> C/(J + m^N) has an R-algebra section sigma. Set Q = J/J^2, T = S tensor_C Omega(C/R) [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-module-base-change], and delta : Q -> T the S-linear conormal differential that sends the class of j to 1 tensor dj. Then for every x in Q, if delta(x) lies in nT, then x lies in nQ. Here the sum of ideals means their join, and mJ means the submodule spanned by products of elements in m and J. No Noetherian hypothesis is assumed; the needed Artin--Rees containment is the explicit hypothesis.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), proof of (4) implies (1); online text at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02HT read 2026-10-13

proof.text: The surjection C -> S pulls n back to m, maps m onto n and identifies S with C/J. For E = C/(J^2 + m^N) and F = C/(J + m^N), the kernel K of E -> F has square zero. Apply the square-zero-section conormal retraction to sigma. Its retraction is F-linear, since the F-action on K is independent of the choice of lift when K^2 = 0. Reduce over F -> k = S/n: tensoring the retraction preserves its left-inverse equation.

The modular law computes the kernel of J -> K as J^2 + (m^N intersect J). Tensoring K with k gives J/(J^2 + (m^N intersect J) + mJ). The assumed containment eliminates the intersection summand, so this is J/(J^2 + mJ) = Q/nQ. The equality uses only the explicit bound, not Noetherianity.

Let D = C/J^2 and m_D be the image of m. Then E = D/(m_D)^N. Apply the differential-mod-power-ideal lemma to D, m_D, exponent N-1 >= 1 and base change further to k. This identifies k tensor_E Omega(E/R) with k tensor_D Omega(D/R). Apply the same lemma to C, J, exponent 1 and then base change C/J -> k. This identifies the latter with k tensor_C Omega(C/R), hence with T/nT by tensor cancellation.

The identifications are induced by quotients and tensor cancellation. On classes represented by j in J, the conormal map sends j to 1 tensor dj, the same as P.cotangentComplex_mk followed by reduction; these classes span the source, so the maps agree. The reduced conormal map is therefore injective. For x with delta(x) in nT its reduced image vanishes; injectivity forces its class in Q/nQ to vanish, namely x in nQ.

theorem truncated_section_conormal_residue_kernel
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalRing S] (P : Extension.{u} R S) [IsLocalRing P.Ring]
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
    (hAR : ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal P.Ring) ^ N •
        (⊤ : Submodule P.Ring P.Ring) ⊓ P.ker) ≤
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal P.Ring) • P.ker)
    (σ : (P.Ring ⧸ (P.ker ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal P.Ring ^ N)) →ₐ[R]
        (P.Ring ⧸ (P.ker ^ 2 ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal P.Ring ^ N)))
    (hσ : (Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ R
        (sup_le_sup (Ideal.pow_le_self (by decide : 2 ≠ 0)) le_rfl)).comp σ =
      AlgHom.id R _) :
    ∀ x : P.Cotangent,
      P.cotangentComplex x ∈
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) • (⊤ : Submodule S P.CotangentSpace) →
        x ∈ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) • (⊤ : Submodule S P.Cotangent)
